subject: Embedding pricing & dimension guidelines for DataPulse (rate card request)

Subject: Embeddings pricing baseline + supported dims/models

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the demo earlier — DataPulse is excited about the latency figures you showed. Procurement asked me to collect a straightforward baseline rate card for embeddings so we can model unit economics for our vector search service. A few specific asks: 

- Pricing unit: do you charge per-vector, per-token, or offer both for embeddings?
- Dimension support: which embedding dimensions do you support (512 / 768 / 1536 / custom)? Are there cost differences by dimension?
- Model variants: which open/verified embedding models are available today (and which are recommended for search vs semantic similarity)?
- Bulk/committed discounts: what thresholds do you offer (monthly vector volumes or $ commit)?

If you can share a one-page PDF or short spreadsheet with baseline per-unit pricing and a quick note about model tradeoffs, procurement will use it to build the TCO. Appreciate a reply this week if possible.

Best,
Harper Lin
Head of AI Platform, DataPulse

From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Harper Lin <harper@datapulse.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-10T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings pricing baseline + supported dims/models

Hi Harper — great to hear and glad the numbers looked promising. Quick answers up-front, plus I'll attach our formal rate card after I loop in pricing.

- Unit options: We publish both per-vector and per-token pricing depending on the model family. Per-vector pricing is common for fixed-dim models (e.g., 1536-dim) and simplifies billing for search. Per-token is used primarily when embedding arises from text preprocessing flows where token counts vary.
- Dimensions: We support 512, 768, and 1536 out of the box; custom dimensions are supported via a model conversion path (there's an engineering lead time and a one-time mapping fee). 1536 is typically recommended for high-accuracy semantic search; 512/768 are good for cheaper, high-throughput use cases. Pricing tiers differ by dimension band — larger dims cost more due to memory and compute.
- Models: Current verified set: redwood-embed-1536, redwood-embed-768, open-sim-512, and a legacy compat model (open-legacy-384). For search we usually recommend redwood-embed-1536 or redwood-embed-768 depending on latency/accuracy tradeoffs.
- Discounts: We offer volume tiers starting at 10M vectors/mo, 100M vectors/mo, and enterprise commits; deeper discounts apply for 12-month or 24-month prepaid commits.

I'll attach a short rate card PDF and a dimension/cost matrix. Rishi — can you confirm the current public list price for 1536 and the standard committed-discount bands?

Next steps: I'll send the formal PDF and a HubSpot deal link. Happy to jump on a procurement call if helpful.

Thanks,
Diego
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood-Embeddings-Ratecard-v1.pdf (pdf)]

2) Do you have a recommended packaging for startups vs enterprise (e.g., packaged SKUs or only custom quotes)?

Harper on behalf of procurement

From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>

Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, procurement@datapulse.ai
Date: 2026-02-16T09:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings pricing baseline + supported dims/models

Harper — answers inline below. We can also set a short call to review the conversion and packaging.

1) Quality delta: Ballpark guidance from internal evals: going from 1536->768 typically reduces nearest-neighbor retrieval recall by ~4–10% depending on dataset complexity (dense, long-tail queries see larger deltas). We can run a 2-week eval on a small sample corpus to quantify for DataPulse — recommended so you get a measured number. I'll propose the eval in the MAP.

2) Packaging: We offer tiered SKUs for startups (self-serve monthly tiers with published prices) and an enterprise track for committed capacity + SLAs (where we provide further discounts, custom dimensions, and dedicated support). For a customer with scale like DataPulse we usually recommend an enterprise commit with a 12–24 month term to lock in pricing and capacity.

3) API call costs: The public list covers the per-vector embedding generation only — there is no additional per-call gateway fee for standard API usage. Any separate charges would be for premium features (long-term retention, extended observability retention) which are optional.

Regarding the 15% introductory credit: We can offer a one-time migration credit equivalent to 10% of the first 3 months' committed spend for a 12-month commit; 15% is slightly above our standard introductory table but I will escalate to commercial approval. If procurement is able to confirm target monthly vectors and preferred term (12 vs 24 months) I can turn this into a firm offer.

I've attached a short mutual action plan (DP_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx) with suggested milestones and the ratecard PDF.

Cheers,
Diego
